rendered.overview: This five-color deck led by [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] chains Lesson spells and elemental bending abilities to draw cards, grow lands into creatures, and ramp through any-color sources. Each waterbend, earthbend, firebend, or airbend triggers Aang's draw ability, and completing all four in one turn transforms him into [[Aang, Master of Elements]] for a burst of life, cards, and damage. Shrines and Allies amplify the engine, turning incidental spellcasting into a growing board of counters and tokens that close out games through combat damage.

strategy: Ramp early with mana rocks and Allies that tap for any color to hit five-color spells on curve.
Cast Lesson spells and bending effects to trigger [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]]'s draw ability.
Use earthbend, waterbend, and firebend abilities to grow lands and creatures into threats with counters.
Accumulate all four elemental triggers in a turn to transform Aang into his back face for a damage burst.
Protect key Allies and Shrines while chaining card draw to refuel after board wipes or attacks.

keep: Hands with a Lesson spell and a way to bend an element to start the draw engine.
sendBack: [[Sol Ring]] with nothing to cast after it stalls out.
A hand with no path to casting a Lesson or bending ability before turn five.

tips.text: Casting [[Earthbending Lesson]] triggers [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] twice, stacking extra +1/+1 counters on a land.
Casting [[The Spirit Oasis]] after [[Guru Pathik]] is out grows a creature while refilling your hand with cards.
[[Katara, the Fearless]] doubles [[Haru, Hidden Talent]]'s earthbend trigger whenever another Ally enters.
Exhaust on [[Jeong Jeong, the Deserter]] copies your next Lesson, letting [[Iroh's Demonstration]] hit twice.

weaknesses: Relies on accumulating multiple elemental triggers in one turn, which can be slow without enablers.
Many effects scale off Shrine or Lesson counts, so early game can feel underwhelming before those build up.
Lacks hard removal outside a few conditional effects, leaving some threats unanswered.

rendered.overview: This Jeskai artifacts deck built around [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] stacks counters onto permanents and spreads them with proliferate. Cheap rocks and artifact creatures enable affinity and improvise discounts, while cards like [[Insight Engine]], [[Lux Cannon]], and [[Tome of Legends]] turn accumulated counters into cards, damage, or extra turns. The deck grinds through repeated proliferate triggers until a payoff like [[Lux Artillery]] or [[Magistrate's Scepter]] closes the game.

strategy: Deploy mana rocks and cheap artifacts early to enable affinity and improvise costs.
Cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and tap it or other permanents to trigger proliferate.
Build counters on [[Insight Engine]], [[Lux Cannon]], and [[Tome of Legends]] for value.
Use [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] and [[Walking Ballista]] to convert counters into cards or damage.
Finish with [[Lux Artillery]]'s counter threshold or repeated extra turns from [[Magistrate's Scepter]].

keep: A hand with an early rock like [[Sol Ring]] or [[Arcane Signet]] plus a payoff.
A hand that can cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] on curve at mana value 3.
sendBack: A hand full of proliferate payoffs but no cheap artifacts to enable them.
A hand relying only on [[Basalt Monolith]] with no way to untap it.

tips.text: Untap [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] with [[Pemmin's Aura]] to proliferate repeatedly in a single turn.
[[Power Conduit]] removes a counter to untap [[Basalt Monolith]] instead of paying its normal cost.
[[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubles proliferate from [[Throne of Geth]], accelerating every counter on board.
[[Deepglow Skate]] doubles charge counters on [[Lux Cannon]], letting it fire immediately.

keyCards.job: Proliferates whenever it gets tapped.
Draws more cards as its counters grow.
Charges up to destroy a permanent.
Stores page counters to cash in for cards.

weaknesses: Relies heavily on cheap artifacts resolving, so early removal or counterspells can derail the plan.
Has few traditional creatures, leaving it vulnerable to wide aggressive boards without enough blockers.
Some engines take several turns to accumulate counters before they produce a payoff.

rendered.overview: This Colorless deck ramps hard through artifact mana and Eldrazi-themed lands to power out big colorless threats, with [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] turning every big spell into a double cascade engine. Board wipes like [[All Is Dust]], [[Perilous Vault]], and the Ugin planeswalkers reset the game while the deck rebuilds faster off ramp and card draw. Eventually the deck floods the board with Eldrazi, Constructs, and tokens that overwhelm with sheer size and Annihilator triggers.

strategy: Ramp early with mana rocks and Eldrazi-support lands to reach big mana quickly.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] to turn high-cost colorless spells into double cascades.
Use board wipes like [[All Is Dust]] or [[Perilous Vault]] to reset when behind.
Deploy Annihilator and removal creatures to pressure opponents and strip permanents.
Refill with artifact draw engines like [[Hedron Archive]] and [[Dreamstone Hedron]] to keep casting threats.

keep: A hand with early ramp like [[Sol Ring]] plus a follow-up spell to cast.
A curve that reaches five or six mana by turn five or six.
sendBack: [[Sol Ring]] with nothing to cast after it stalls out.
A hand full of expensive spells with no ramp to reach them.

tips.text: Casting [[Artisan of Kozilek]] off [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] can cascade into a reanimation chain.
Sacrifice two artifacts like [[Hangarback Walker]] tokens to return [[Metalwork Colossus]] from the graveyard.
[[Spine of Ish Sah]] bounces to hand when it dies, letting [[Mystic Forge]] recast it off the top repeatedly.
[[Forsaken Monument]] doubles colorless mana, letting [[Basalt Monolith]] untap itself for free.

keyCards.job: Grants cascade to big colorless spells.
Refills hand and counters spells by discard.
Exiles colored permanents and can refill the board.
Lets the deck cast spells straight off the library.
Produces a burst of colorless mana.
Becomes cheap and recurs from the graveyard.
Discounts Eldrazi and tutors one up late.

weaknesses: Relies on reaching high mana values, so early disruption of ramp can stall the whole plan.
Few sources of colored removal mean answers to hexproof or protected threats are limited.
Top-heavy curve can lead to clunky hands if ramp spells are drawn too late.

rendered.overview: This Naya deck builds toward casting big Dinosaurs and attacking with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]], whose combat damage triggers put more Dinosaurs straight onto the battlefield. Cost reducers like [[Knight of the Stampede]] and [[Otepec Huntmaster]] get huge threats out early, while Enrage creatures such as [[Ripjaw Raptor]] and [[Polyraptor]] reward getting hit. The deck wins by overwhelming the board with trampling giants.

strategy: Ramp with creatures and lands to reach a critical mass of mana.
Deploy cost-reduced Dinosaurs using [[Knight of the Stampede]] and [[Otepec Huntmaster]].
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to cascade more Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
Trigger Enrage creatures like [[Ripjaw Raptor]] and [[Polyraptor]] via fights and pings.
Close games with trampling attackers backed by [[Garruk's Uprising]] and [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger]].

keep: A hand with a two-drop ramp creature leading into a four-drop threat.
Early plays plus a way to reach eight mana for [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]].
sendBack: A hand full of expensive Dinosaurs with no early plays before turn four.
Hands relying on a single land-fetch spell and nothing else to do.

tips.text: [[Marauding Raptor]] pings [[Polyraptor]] for 2 damage, triggering Enrage to create a copy token each time a creature enters.
[[Boxing Ring]] fights deal damage to [[Bellowing Aegisaur]], triggering Enrage to counter up every other creature you control.
[[Fight Rigging]] can hideaway [[Thrasta, Tempest's Roar]] and cast it free once a creature reaches power 7.
[[Forerunner of the Empire]] entering a Dinosaur lets [[Marauding Raptor]] ping it for extra damage and growth.

keyCards.job: Attacks to cheat Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
Pings creatures to trigger Enrage abilities.
Replaces itself whenever it takes damage.
Multiplies itself each time it is damaged.
Grows a creature and casts a hidden card free.
Becomes a cheap hasty trampler late in turns.
Discounts every Dinosaur spell you cast.
Grants trample and draws off big creatures.

weaknesses: Relies heavily on resolving and attacking with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to function at full speed.
Has few ways to interact with noncreature permanents or stop a combo outside creature fights.
Vulnerable to board wipes since the plan centers on committing many creatures at once.

rendered.overview: This Red Goblin tribal deck swarms the board with token-makers and payoff creatures, then multiplies that army by tapping [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] for a wave of 1/1 Goblins. From there it pivots into burn, sacrifice outlets like [[Goblin Bombardment]], and damage-doubling pingers such as [[Sparksmith]] and [[Spikeshot Goblin]] to close the game through combat or direct damage.

strategy: Ramp with artifacts and Goblin mana dorks like [[Skirk Prospector]] to accelerate into [[Krenko, Mob Boss]].
Deploy early Goblin tokens with [[Dragon Fodder]] and [[Mogg War Marshal]] to build board presence.
Resolve [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and tap it to flood the battlefield with Goblin tokens.
Pump the team with [[Goblin Chieftain]] and [[Goblin Warchief]] then swing for lethal with haste.
Use sacrifice outlets like [[Goblin Bombardment]] or [[Pashalik Mons]] to convert extra Goblins into direct damage.

keep: A hand with early ramp like [[Skirk Prospector]] and a path to turn 4.
Goblin token makers such as [[Dragon Fodder]] alongside a couple of lands.
sendBack: A hand that can't reach five mana for [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] without help.
A hand full of expensive burn spells but no way to make Goblins.

tips.text: [[Goblin Chieftain]] gives every token from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] haste so they can swing immediately.
Sacrifice extra Goblins to [[Goblin Bombardment]] while [[Sparksmith]] scales its damage with your Goblin count.
Sacrifice spare Goblins to [[Skirk Prospector]] for mana or to [[Goblin Grenade]] for a burst of damage.
Casting [[Firebolt]] from hand or flashback triggers [[Guttersnipe]] for extra damage to opponents.

keyCards.job: Floods the board with Goblin tokens on a tap.'
Discounts Goblin spells and grants haste to the swarm.
Pumps and hastes every other Goblin you control.
Turns spare Goblins into direct damage.
Pings for each Goblin that dies and makes more.
Deals damage scaling with your Goblin count.
Punishes opponents whenever you cast instants or sorceries.
Converts extra Goblins into mana for Krenko.

weaknesses: Many small Goblin tokens die easily to single-target removal, slowing the overall plan.
